 Article Tech & AI OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for Secure AI Agent Payments
 By Daisy Hawker November 15, 2026 undefined mins Share this article Prioritise Us on Google Share this article Prioritise Us on Google OpenAI, Visa, American Express and Mastercard come together to create ChatGPT Wallet. Credit: Getty Visa's Rubail Birwadker explains how ChatGPT Wallet, launched in collaboration with American Express, Visa and Mastercard, connects AI to user approval 
 In the race for agentic AI commerce, OpenAI has announced the launch of ChatGPT Wallet, a payment tool that lets AI agents buy goods on behalf of users without seeing their actual card details.
 ChatGPT Wallet was created in partnership with American Express , Mastercard and Visa , and requires a biometric security check for each purchase.
 In a blog for OpenAI, Rubail Birwadker , Head of Global Growth, Visa, says: “To deliver on the promise of agentic commerce, consumers, businesses and banks all need to trust the process.
 “We’re partnering with OpenAI to bring Visa’s trusted infrastructure to the experience, helping connect user-approved purchases with the systems businesses already use.”
 According to OpenAI, the key differentiator for ChatGPT wallet is that it is the first wallet that lets agents pay without access to a user’s real card information.
 Rubail Birwadker says the partnership will bring OpenAI's infrastructure to ChatGPT Wallet. Credit: LinkedIn Key facts about ChatGPT Wallet Works with American Express, Mastercard and Visa cards 
 Launches to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US 
 Replaces real card details with payment tokens 
 Requires biometric approval for every purchase 
 Keeps card rewards and protections for eligible disputes 
 Runs through dots in ChatGPT. 
 How ChatGPT Wallet works
 Users add a card once and then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details. The card is stored securely and kept separate from the user’s ChatGPT subscription payment method and any gift card or prepaid balance.
 After approval, the payment network provides a payment token, a substitute for the user’s actual card details. The token comes with its own card number, security code and expiry date.
 The payment is charged to the user’s selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing the real details with the business or agent.
 Additionally, before each purchase, the user reviews the merchant, items, total and selected card, along with any shipping or recurring-payment terms.
 Then, users approve it with a biometric check such as Face ID or Touch ID.
 Each approval creates a clear record of the purchase the user authorised the agent to make. After approval, the dot continues checkout and reports the result.
 The first American Express Agentic Commerce Experiences integration
 Aside from biometric verification, ChatGPT Wallet marks another first by being the first integration under American Express Agentic Commerce Experiences, meaning Eligible Card Members can use their Amex Card while reviewing and approving each purchase.
 Luke Gebb , Executive Vice President and Head of Global Innovation at American Express, says: “Working with OpenAI, we’re bringing the trust, security and control of American Express payments into new AI-powered shopping experiences.
 “ChatGPT Wallet marks our first American Express Agentic Commerce Experiences integration, enabling eligible Card Members to use their Amex Card while reviewing and approving each purchase.
 “We’re excited to learn together from this early phase and build toward bringing these experiences to more Card Members over time.”
 Luke Gebb is the Executive Vice President and Head of Global Innovation at American Express. Credit: LinkedIn Working with OpenAI, we’re bringing the trust, security and control of American Express payments into new AI-powered shopping experiences
 Luke Gebb, Executive Vice President and Head of Global Innovation at American Express 
 Delegated purchases ahead
 OpenAI expects users to delegate purchases entirely to their agent over time. They would set clear parameters such as spending limits, purchase categories or time periods.
 Those purchases would be pre-approved with enhanced safeguards that build on today’s protections. These include biometric checks and clear records of authorisation.
 For now, every purchase needs the user’s approval. Users who change their mind before approval can decline the request, and cancelling a completed order means contacting the merchant.
 Further commerce partners for OpenAI
 Stripe co-developed the Agentic Commerce Protocol with OpenAI and supported the September 2025 launch of Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, which began with Etsy sellers. Its shared payment tokens let ChatGPT initiate a payment without exposing the buyer’s credentials. The protocol gives merchants a standard route into agentic commerce.
 PayPal adopted the Agentic Commerce Protocol in October 2025 to power in-chat payments within ChatGPT. The move extends agentic commerce to PayPal’s global merchant network. President and Chief Executive Officer Alex Chriss says more than 400 million people use PayPal to shop.
 Shopify was named by OpenAI in September 2025 as the next platform for Instant Checkout after Etsy, with its more than 1 million merchants set to follow. Brands including Glossier, SKIMS, Spanx and Vuori were listed. Merchants pay a small fee on completed purchases made through ChatGPT.
